newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to protect financial sector - Suharto.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to protect financial sector - Suharto.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto has said that the country will continue to restrict foreign investors in the financial services sector, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Friday.
"If we open the financial services too much, we will lose because we are not strong enough," Suharto was quoted as saying by Bank Bukopin president Muchtar Mandala after a meeting with the president.

The meeting was to brief Suharto on preparation for the Asia-Europe Business Meeting which begins in Paris on Saturday, the Jakarta Post said. It is a follow-up to the Asia-Europe summit held in Bangkok earlier this year.

Muchtar, who is part of a six-member Indonesian delegation going to Paris, said that continued restrictions in the banking, insurance and financial sectors were a major source of contention with potential European financial investors.
"France, Belgium and the others stress that they have none of their banks operating here," Muchtar was quoted as saying by the Jakarta Post.
Currently, only ten wholly foreign-owned banks operate in Indonesia, including Standard Chartered Bank, Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp's HongKong Bank, ABN AMRO and Deutsche Bank.

Muchtar said that Indonesia needs to protect the many small domestic banks that exist since the government initiated a series of economic deregulations in the late 1980s to open up the banking sector.
There are seven state-owned banks in Indonesia, 77 private foreign exchange (forex) and 88 private non-forex banks, as well as 27 development banks and 31 joint ventures.
